layers.general_terms: Microsoft's 'Use of Microsoft copyrighted content' page (screenshot section) permits screenshots in videos on conditions: no alteration except resizing, no use of portions, no third-party content, no identifiable individuals, full product names, and the statement 'Used with permission from Microsoft.'
layers.status: unresolved: whether this use meets Microsoft's guideline is a legal judgement, not a fact this ticket can settle

guideline_fit_notes: Resize: the frame scales the guest screen 2x with nearest-neighbour. The guideline allows resizing.
Portions: the frame crops the capturer's 1920x1080 host capture to the full 640x480 Windows 3.1 guest screen. Whether this counts as a whole Windows screenshot or as a 'portion' is open.
Third-party content: present in the uncropped original (wallpaper artwork, VirtualBox), absent from the frame.
Identifiable individuals: none seen in the guest screen. The host wallpaper is a drawn character, and it is cropped out.
Appearance: the guest uses a non-default Windows colour scheme (black active title bar with red frame) and a cyan patterned wallpaper. Resizing aside, nothing in the guest screen was altered.
proposed_credit_text: Screenshot: Matthew Paul Argall, via Internet Archive (archive.org/details/solitaire-windows-3.1). Microsoft Windows 3.1 and Microsoft Solitaire are products of Microsoft Corporation.
conditional_credit_note: Add this only if rights review confirms the use meets Microsoft's screenshot guideline. It is not claimed now.
review_questions: Is the Windows 3.1 Solitaire still cleared for use under Microsoft's published screenshot guideline, given the frame is a crop of a host capture down to the full guest screen? If not, is fair use/fair dealing commentary relied on, or is the shot dropped?
Is the capturer's informal collection statement (credit preferred) enough for the capture layer, or should written permission be sought from the capturer before release?
